Label: Coach's note - The push press
Text: Shoulder to Overhead permits a dip and drive. That is worth twenty to thirty per cent over a strict press for most trained athletes, which is why every benchmark built on strict press understates this event. Dip shallow and vertical, drive through the whole foot, and move the head through as the bar passes. The legs start the lift and the arms finish it.

Label: The standard - SkiErg
Text: The damper may be adjusted before and during the workout. Find your setting in training and write it down, since venue machines vary and it saves a decision on the day. Most athletes settle between 5 and 8 at a stroke rate of 34 to 42.

Label: Score impact
Text: Your score is the sum of three placings, and the lowest total wins. The best available result in a zone is one point; the worst is the size of the field. Strong results are capped at one point, while weak ones are not, which is why consistency matters.

Label: Kit - What you may use
Text: Permitted on the strength floor: chalk (bring your own), knee sleeves, elbow sleeves, weightlifting belt, weightlifting shoes, wrist wraps. Banned: lifting straps, hand grips, knee wraps, elbow wraps, and any supportive suit or briefs.

Label: No rep - Dumbbells
Text: Dumbbells must be placed on the floor once your reps are complete, and dropping them is a no rep. Letting go is a natural reaction at the end of a hard set, so it is worth practising the controlled finish in training.

Label: The number
Text: The Endurance Zone cap is fixed. Whatever time the run takes is subtracted from your ski time, and only the ski scores. That single fact is why the zone is one continuous effort, not two events.

Label: Coach's note - Easy means easy
Text: Running easy sessions too quickly turns a recovery day into a moderate one, which tends to leave you flat for the sessions that matter later in the week. The test is full sentences without pausing for breath. If in doubt, slow down.

Label: The standard - Deadlift
Text: Hands must be outside the knees. Sumo deadlifts are not permitted. Double overhand, mixed and hook grip are all allowed. The Base phase is a good time to settle into a conventional stance, rather than adjusting to it later in the plan.

Label: Coach's note - Hip hinge, not arm pull
Text: The SkiErg is driven by the hips. Load the hinge, snap it closed, and let the arms follow through. If your arms fatigue before your trunk does, the pull is coming from the arms, which is difficult to sustain for twelve minutes.

Label: The number
Text: What one second of run time is worth on the ski, at a 2:00 per 500 m pace. Save forty-five seconds on the buy-in and you gain roughly 187 metres of score. Nothing else in this sport converts so directly.

Label: Kit - Lifting straps are banned
Text: You may not use straps or hand grips. That makes grip a genuine limiter on your deadlift and on the sandbag carry. That is why Tuesday carries a grip block every week, as competition preparation rather than general accessory work.

Label: No rep - Sandbag carry
Text: Both feet must clearly pass the turn line and the finish line. Touching the line does not count. Turning early is easy to do when breathing hard, so it is worth running through the line rather than to it.

Label: From the floor - Transition habit
Text: The first thirty seconds off the run is where the time gained on the buy-in is most easily given back. Reset posture within three strides of reaching the machine, take one deliberate breath, and start at pace rather than pausing to gather yourself.

Label: Score impact
Text: Rank points are cheapest where the field is densest. The same improvement is worth roughly three times as many placings from mid-pack as it is from the top seven per cent. Placings are easiest to gain where you currently sit furthest back.

Label: The standard - Back squat
Text: The hip crease must pass below the top of the knee. A rep only counts when you return to full extension of hips and knees. Depth is judged rather than estimated, so it is worth filming a set this week to check.

Label: No rep - Back squat - the walk-in
Text: On your final rep you must be fully extended and given the rep verbally before you walk the bar back to the rack. Walk early and the rep does not count. Re-rack it and you start again from zero. This is one of the more costly errors available in the Strength Zone, and it is entirely avoidable.

Label: Coach's note - Bench press endurance
Text: DB bench press was not in the 2026 format, so it is new to most people entering in 2027. Running, HYROX and general conditioning backgrounds rarely build horizontal pressing endurance. Thirty reps is a local endurance demand rather than a strength one, and it responds quickly to targeted work.

Label: The number
Text: The time penalty for letting go of the erg handles in a manner that could damage the machine. Bring the handle high and release it gently, in training as well as in competition.

Label: Kit - Footwear and sleeves
Text: Footwear must be worn. One pair of knee sleeves only - not two, and they may not be rolled to increase thickness. Headphones and earbuds are not permitted anywhere on the competition floor, so if you usually train with music it is worth doing some sessions without it.

Label: From the floor - Pacing the buy-in
Text: Common advice suggests the first four minutes should feel almost easy. In this format that reduces the ski time available, which is where the score comes from. Run the buy-in at or above your 10 km race pace from the start.

Label: Score impact
Text: An athlete who wins two zones and finishes fortieth in the third scores 42. An athlete who finishes twelfth, fourteenth and fifteenth scores 41 and beats them. A strong result in one zone cannot be carried across to offset a weak one.

Label: Coach's note - Deload honestly
Text: The purpose of a deload is to let accumulated fatigue clear so the next phase starts on a recovered athlete, which is why the reduced load is worth keeping to. Feeling good on a light week is a sign it is working rather than evidence that more was needed.

Label: The standard - Ground to overhead
Text: A snatch or a clean and jerk are both permitted. If you split snatch, both feet must return in line under your body while the dumbbell is locked out. Pick one method and train it, since switching technique under fatigue tends to cost reps.

Label: The number
Text: The transition tax. Ski two minutes at ten seconds per 500 m slower than steady after a hard run and you lose about 39 metres. Set against the 187 metres a faster buy-in earns you, the tax is roughly one fifth of the benefit. Run hard.

Label: Kit - Collars and plates
Text: Collars must be placed outside the plates on every barbell lift, warm-ups included. Unused plates must be inside the rig and off the lifting area. Small details, but a judge will stop you for them and the clock keeps running.

Label: No rep - Ground to overhead - the non-lifting hand
Text: Your free hand may not make contact with your legs or any other part of your body during the rep. Bracing a hand on the thigh under fatigue is a natural reaction and it is a no rep, so it is worth training with the free arm out.

Label: From the floor - Kit check
Text: Sorting the logistics early is easier than doing it in week twelve. Chalk is yours to bring. Pack a spare pair of shoes. Venue floors vary and grip on the sandbag carry matters more than people expect.

Label: Coach's note - The week behind you
Text: Look back before looking forward. If the ski intervals faded more than they did in week one and the lifts have stalled, fatigue has accumulated faster than it has cleared. In that case, repeating this deload is a better option than starting the Development phase.

Label: The standard - Deadlift - the pause
Text: Maximum pause between reps is five seconds, and if you set the bar down your hands must stay on it. Let go and the count restarts at zero. It is worth rehearsing your triple as three singles, with your hands staying on the bar throughout.

Label: Coach's note - Ski pace discipline
Text: The zone scores total metres, so an even effort generally produces more than a fast opening followed by a fade. Set your target pace and hold it. Negative split by a second or two if anything.

Label: The number
Text: What fifteen seconds per kilometre is worth. Run the 3 km buy-in that much faster and you gain forty-five seconds of ski time, which is roughly 187 metres of score. This is why the Endurance Zone is one twenty-four minute effort, not two events.

Label: Score impact
Text: Missing both deadlift windows affects more than the component itself. The Strength total falls, and with it the Strength placing, potentially by a considerable margin. Because the best result available in each of the other zones is one point, there is limited scope to recover the difference.

Label: No rep - Sandbag - dropping early
Text: If the bag is dropped or thrown before both feet have clearly passed the line, you must pick it up, move it back and cross again. It is easy to set the bag down on the line rather than beyond it when fatigued, so carry through.

Label: Kit - Chalk
Text: Bring your own. It is permitted and it is not provided. With straps not permitted, chalk is the only grip aid available on the deadlift and the sandbag.

Label: From the floor - Between zones
Text: The three zones sit inside a two and a half hour window, so what you eat and drink between them has more effect than the morning meal. Rehearsing it during the Specific phase means nothing on the day is being tried for the first time.

Label: Coach's note - The repeat-triple
Text: Two near-maximal triples sixty seconds apart is trainable, and rarely addressed directly. Watch the drop from the first triple to the second rather than the weight on the first. Closing that gap improves the average.

Label: The standard - Sandbag carry - the pick
Text: The bag must be taken from the ground. Any method of getting it to a bear hug or to the shoulder is permitted. Both are worth practising. A shoulder carry is usually quicker over 30 m but harder to secure once grip is fatigued.

Label: The number
Text: Total working time across all three zones, spread over a two and a half hour window with recovery between. This is why carbohydrate loading suits this event less well than it does longer races. Glycogen is unlikely to be the limiting factor, and loading tends to add water weight and gastrointestinal load.

Label: Kit - Belts and wraps
Text: Weightlifting belts, wrist wraps, elbow sleeves and knee sleeves are all permitted. Knee wraps and elbow wraps are not. If you plan to compete in a belt, train in it on your heavy days rather than introducing it on the day.

Label: No rep - Deadlift - the finish
Text: The rep is credited when hips and knees reach full extension and your head and shoulders are behind the bar. Stopping just short is easy to do under fatigue, so stand fully upright and hold the position briefly.

Label: From the floor - Ski damper
Text: The damper may be adjusted before and during the workout, though every second spent adjusting is a second not skiing. Set it in your warm-up and leave it alone.

Label: Score impact
Text: Consistency across the three zones matters more than an outstanding result in any one of them. Every zone gets dedicated weekly attention in this plan, which suits the way rank-sum scoring rewards balance.

Label: From the floor - Rehearsal, not workout
Text: Today's session is data collection. Run the buy-in at the pace you intend to race and record every 500 m ski split. Try not to adjust mid-session to protect the number. A rehearsal that shows a genuine result is more useful than one that flatters.

Label: Coach's note - Reading the decay curve
Text: If your first two ski minutes are poor and you recover, you have a transition problem, and that is trainable. If the pace decays steadily throughout, you have a ski endurance problem and you need more of Tuesday.

Label: The number
Text: How much ski pace you can afford to lose by running the buy-in thirty seconds per kilometre faster, and still score the same. Most athletes lose between six and twelve per cent moving to a 5 km effort. The trade is comfortably positive.

Label: The standard - Back squat - continuity
Text: As long as the bar stays in the back rack position, your reps do not need to be consecutive. But if you re-rack or dump the bar, the score is void and you start again. That means you can pause and reset between reps of a heavy double. Use it.

Label: No rep - Burpees over the bench
Text: Chest must clearly touch the ground on every rep. Chest contact is usually the first standard to slip thirty reps into MetCon X, and judges watch for it.

Label: Kit - Shoes
Text: Weightlifting shoes are permitted in the Strength Zone, though one pair of stable trainers across all three zones suits most athletes better. Changing shoes costs time between zones and adds another thing to remember.

Label: Coach's note - Sunday audit
Text: If Wednesday's deadlift gap widened rather than narrowed, and Saturday's ski faded more than five per cent, you are accumulating fatigue faster than you are clearing it. In that case the Week 8 deload is worth taking in full rather than pushing through.

Label: Coach's note - Taper the deload
Text: Intensity stays and volume halves, so this is a sharpening week rather than a rest week. The Specific phase depends on arriving recovered, so week nine is worth reaching in good shape.

Label: Score impact
Text: Field size sets the downside. In a hundred-athlete field, a last place in one zone costs a hundred points, which is difficult to recover elsewhere. That is why the pacing guidance here favours protecting a solid result over chasing a peak one.

Label: The number
Text: How much more a given improvement is worth in placings from the middle of the field than from the top seven per cent. Giving your weakest zone the most attention returns more placings than the same effort spent on a strong one.

Label: The standard - Run laps
Text: Completing the full number of laps is the athlete's responsibility, and a miscount means the distance does not count. Know the lap length before you start and count deliberately.

Label: No rep - Ground to overhead - alternating
Text: In the ATHX division you must alternate arms after each successful rep. If you are given a no rep, that rep must be repeated with the same arm. Losing track of which arm you are on costs reps, so it is worth establishing a rhythm you can hold when tired.

Label: Kit - The bag
Text: Pack it the night before every simulation, not just for the competition. Chalk, sleeves, belt, shoes, food, bottle. The simulations rehearse the whole day, and packing is part of what they are for.

Label: From the floor - Warm-up architecture
Text: Five minutes per lift includes your warm-up. That means everything must be front-loaded before the clock starts. Arrive already warm through shoulders, hips and posterior chain, with the exact ramp rehearsed.

Label: From the floor - The compressed ramp
Text: Five minutes covers a maximal Shoulder to Overhead from a standing start, which allows for two or three loaded singles and the attempt. Write the ramp down: bar, then three loads, then the attempt, and practise it against a timer each week from here.

Label: Coach's note - Attempt selection
Text: Open your first deadlift window at a weight you are ninety-five per cent confident of - typically ninety to ninety-three per cent of a fresh triple, adjusted down for the squat that precedes it. Window two is informed by how window one felt. Fast means add five to ten kilos. A grind means repeat.

Label: The number
Text: What a missed deadlift window costs you. The score averages two attempts, so a miss contributes zero to that average. In conventional max testing a miss costs nothing, whereas here it costs half the component, which is why the opening attempt is best kept conservative.

Label: The standard - Shoulder to overhead
Text: The 2027 standards had not been published when this book went to press. The 2026 strict press standard required full lockout with hips and knees extended and the bar over the centre of the body. Expect the same finish position with the dip and drive now permitted. Confirm against the official standards before you compete.

Label: No rep - Row calories
Text: You must complete the full required calories before coming off the seat. The monitor, not your count, is what the judge reads. Standing before the monitor shows full calories is a common way to lose a good MetCon time.

Label: Kit - What is in your bag on the day
Text: Chalk. One pair of knee sleeves, unrolled. Belt. Wrist wraps if you use them. Shoes. Food and drink for the gaps between zones. Not in your bag: straps, hand grips, knee wraps, headphones. All banned.

Label: Score impact
Text: Compare your numbers against published results rather than your own training history. The useful question is where your total would have placed. Doing that for all three zones shows where your discretionary training time is best spent.

Label: Coach's note - The MetCon crux
Text: Sandbag squats into an immediate carry is where the workout is decided. Same grip, same trunk, no relief between them. One full exhale on each squat ascent, without holding your breath at the bottom.

Label: The number
Text: MetCon X is bookended by rows, and they are the only elements where you control pace with real precision. Set off at an effort you could hold for the whole piece, since the opening row is where time is most easily overspent.

Label: The standard - Sandbag carry distance
Text: Thirty metres is fifteen out and fifteen back. Both feet must clearly pass the turn line. Individual athletes carry 30 m. Pairs carry 60 m with a changeover, and the second athlete must start from behind the designated line.

Label: From the floor - Between-zone fuelling
Text: Thirty to forty minutes between zones is enough for 30 to 40 g of easily digested carbohydrate and fluid, and not enough for a meal. Rehearse exactly what you will take. Competition day is not the time to discover something does not sit well.

Label: No rep - Bench press lockout
Text: Every rep needs full elbow extension. Under fatigue the last few centimetres are the first thing to go. Counting in blocks of ten, resetting the breathing between them, works better than a continuous thirty.

Label: Kit - Grip without straps
Text: With straps banned, hook grip or mixed grip is your only option on a heavy deadlift triple. If you use hook grip, chalk heavily. If you use mixed grip, alternate which hand supinates across your training sets.

Label: Coach's note - Commit the plan to paper
Text: Write your deadlift attempt weights, your buy-in pace and your MetCon opening row split on a card and put it in your bag. Decisions made calmly this week tend to be better than the same ones made under fatigue on the floor.

Label: From the floor - Simulate the day, not the sessions
Text: Warm-up timing, food between zones, kit changes, chalk and where your bag goes. The logistics are as much a part of the day as the sessions. Every problem found today is one you will not meet on the floor.

Label: Score impact
Text: The best available result in a zone is one point, while the worst is the size of the field, so the tactical decisions from here favour protecting the result. Hold the opening run to your rehearsed pace, use a sandbag load you can control, and avoid taking risks in any single zone.

Label: The number
Text: Under rank-sum scoring, balance across zones tends to outscore specialisation, sometimes by a single point. Three solid placings will usually finish ahead of two wins and a poor result.

Label: Coach's note - The last hard week
Text: From here the aim shifts from building fitness to preserving it, since twelve days is not long enough to add much. Train this week fully, and from then on additional work is unlikely to help.

Label: The standard - Erg handles
Text: Handles must not be released in a way that could damage the machine. Bring them high and release gently, or hand over in pairs. The penalty is thirty seconds. That is a large number in a time-scored workout.

Label: Kit - Two of everything
Text: Spare shoes, spare chalk and spare food. Venue conditions vary and so do plans. It is also worth knowing where the venue is, when you need to arrive and what the parking is like, since the day starts well before the first zone.

Label: Coach's note - Unload begins
Text: From tomorrow, volume comes down while intensity stays. That will feel like less work, which is the intention. The work is already banked, and the taper is what lets it show.

Label: Coach's note - Trust the taper
Text: Short, sharp sessions finished before you feel like stopping. These should feel comfortably fast rather than hard. If it feels hard, reducing Wednesday further is a better response than pushing on.

Label: Kit - Damper setting
Text: Write your ski damper number down today and put it with your attempt card. Venue machines vary, and knowing your setting saves time at the start of a scored zone.

Label: The standard - No eccentric work
Text: Heavy eccentric loading is the main cause of microtrauma and lingering soreness, so it stops seven days out. Lower under control today, without chasing slow negatives. The focus is concentric.

Label: Coach's note - The day before the day before
Text: Rest is the session today, and there is nothing to gain from testing yourself. Nothing done today will improve Sunday, and a hard session could affect it.

Label: From the floor - Shakeout
Text: Twenty minutes in total, all of it easy, finishing while you still feel fresh. The purpose is blood flow and familiarity rather than fitness, so keeping it easy matters.

Label: From the floor - The night before
Text: Pack the bag, write the card and set two alarms. Eat normally, since there is no loading protocol for this event. Then leave it there. The work is done.

Label: Score impact
Text: Lowest total placing wins, so three solid zones will usually finish ahead of two excellent ones and a poor one. Open the deadlift conservatively, run the buy-in at your rehearsed pace, control the opening row, and race the rest.
